passages.heading: Title
passages.text: ELX-NSCLC-01: an open-label, single-arm study of the investigational agent ELX-101 in adults with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer. This protocol is invented for software verification; its thresholds are engineering fixtures, not clinical recommendations.

passages.heading: Inclusion criteria
passages.text: Participants must meet all of the following criteria.
Age 18 to 75 years, inclusive, on the date of eligibility assessment.
Histologically or cytologically confirmed non-small-cell lung cancer.
Locally advanced disease (stage IIIB or IIIC) that is not amenable to curative-intent treatment, or metastatic disease (stage IVA or IVB).
Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1, assessed within 28 days before eligibility assessment.
Absolute neutrophil count of at least 1.5 × 10⁹/L within 14 days before eligibility assessment.
Haemoglobin of at least 9.0 g/dL within 14 days before eligibility assessment.
No more than two prior systemic anticancer treatment regimens.
Participants who received prior systemic anticancer therapy must have received the last dose at least 21 days before eligibility assessment.

passages.heading: Exclusion criteria
passages.text: Participants meeting any of the following criteria are excluded.
Active infection requiring systemic antimicrobial therapy at the time of eligibility assessment.
Untreated or symptomatic central nervous system (CNS) metastases. Participants with treated, asymptomatic and radiologically stable CNS metastases may enrol.

passages.heading: Assessment conventions
passages.text: These conventions apply to every criterion in sections 5.1 and 5.2.
Eligibility is assessed on the eligibility assessment date using information recorded on or before that date. An observation window includes its first day and the assessment date.

A laboratory value or performance status is the latest result within its window. Results recorded on the same date that disagree leave the criterion unresolved, and an older result never replaces a newer one.

Prior systemic anticancer regimens are counted once each, however many encounters record them. A regimen count or washout is established only when a treatment-history review within 28 days before the assessment date records the history as complete.

A condition is absent only when the record states that it is absent; a note that does not mention a condition is not evidence of its absence. Disease stage and histology are the latest recorded at any time; tumour-board conclusions count within 60 days, CNS findings within 28 days and infection findings within 14 days.
